canonical_topic: Standard forward power blocks referenced per tolling leg (peak/off-peak/weekend)
definition: Each monthly leg of a tolling agreement is typically valued/hedged against the specific power block products actually traded in that local forward market.
core_idea: Commonly traded forward power contracts are peak power (5×16), off-peak power (7×8), and weekend power (2×16), so a single tolling leg often depends on several distinct instruments at once, which combined with time-of-year effects multiplies the number of largely uncorrelated exposures across the contract's life.
key_points: 5×16 power = peak block (5 weekdays, 16 hours per day).
7×8 power = off-peak block (7 days, 8 hours per day, i.e. nighttime).
2×16 power = weekend block (2 days, 16 hours per day).
Each tolling leg can depend on a mix of these instruments rather than one flat power price.
relationships: Extends the non-fungibility/underlying-instruments concept within a single leg
trading_implications: Hedging a tolling leg requires trading the specific block products the local forward market offers, not a single generic power price
caveats: Assuming a single power price index can hedge an entire monthly leg
